question: Should the permanent core policy use allow/deny patterns or typed read/write roots, and may its first version explicitly exclude arbitrary exec-mediated filesystem access?
rationale: The two open candidates encode materially different public configuration and security guarantees, and automation cannot safely choose which permanent contract OpenClaw should support.

options.title: Typed roots, file tools first
options.body: Use explicit file/directory roots with read-only/read-write permissions across all host file and media paths, while documenting arbitrary exec as outside the guarantee.

options.title: Allow and deny patterns
options.body: Use deny-wins path patterns with rigorous normalization, symlink, and operation semantics, while still treating arbitrary exec separately.

options.title: Require OS enforcement
options.body: Defer granular core policy until a sandbox backend can enforce the same boundary for shell-mediated filesystem access.

recommendation.title: Typed roots, file tools first
recommendation.body: Use explicit file/directory roots with read-only/read-write permissions across all host file and media paths, while documenting arbitrary exec as outside the guarantee.

likelyOwner.reason: The original workspace-only contract and prior maintainer-side review make steipete the strongest available owner for selecting its successor.
